title: Return Hook
designBriefSource: The requested six-family planning batch; private prompt retained outside distribution.
goal: Collect the gem in the small chamber at (5,5,0).
stageDependency: Move the L left and upward -> dock its offset tip across the void -> lift the target out of its notch -> reach its newly usable side -> shift it right and collect the gem.
planningBurden: The visible working tip solves an input problem that the player cannot solve directly; contact alone still leaves the chamber blocked.
changedConstraints: A three-member lateral L replaces the source rear-contact C.
A flange blocks downward disposal and a ceiling prevents another upward target shift.
The remaining task uses a newly reachable target input instead of ending at contact.
physicalScope: One 16 by 16 room; ordinary pinned official engine; all initial actors at elevation zero.

difficulty.qualification: An author estimate from dependent operations and planning tradeoffs, not calibrated human difficulty.

limits: Tool movement, target movement, lateral transfer, independent preparation and target work after every first-contact history pass exhausted restrictions.
The tool can be retired after its release; continued motion of that tool is not claimed necessary.
No global minimality or uniqueness of the L shape is claimed.
